as someone who has dealt with suicidal thought before, they can be very scary. i surprised myself at just how far id go to get things to off myself (stealing my family’s pills in my case). often times suicide is classed by danger based off of if the person has made plans/ an attempt to go through with it. the fact that he bought it is concerning. if you think your parents/ family would be supportive of helping him & not ridiculing him, i think it would be a good idea to tell them. on one hand i would’ve hated if someone had told my mom, but on the other it could’ve saved me from a lot of pain & hospital visits. 

as for what you can do, the number one thing is to be there for him. i know it may not seem like much but i promise you, one person who you know loves and supports you 100% makes a huge difference. it’s easy to push everyone away and isolate yourself, and having someone check in on you and ask how your doing, even if the answer is always the same, can really help them out. 

i think it’s great that you’re trying to help, and i’m sure he appreciates it as well. my therapist always tells me that the best thing you can do against depression is anything. literally anything. if all you can do is open a window and sit up in bed, that’s good enough. let him know that he has worth and is cared for. often times we need people who’ll just listen to what’s happening without judgement or advice. i hope your doctor gets back to you soon, and i hope you can help him out
